newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The Athens Stock Exchange rose to its highest levels in three years yesterday when the general price index closed at 1,125 points, a rise of 3.0 percent, the highest since 1995. Intense buying interest was centred on banking and industrials.
--Two foreign banks are reported to be interested in the sale of the Bank of Central Greece as the creation of a new playing field for both the banking and insurance sectors gets under way.
--The government is considering legislative reforms that will allow companies facing problems to freeze debts to the state for 12 months.

--The government's action plan on a new round of farmers' protests foresees a speedy attempt to avert road blockades by moving on decisions already taken to resolve problems. Officials at the agriculture ministry and the Agricultural Bank are already in feverish meetings with regional farmers' groups.
IMERISIA

--The advent of banking shares - rising close to 5.0 percent - powered the general price index to new heights yesterday. Low interest rates, the impending OTE share float, and expected banknig profits are the main reason behind yesterday's rally.
--Sources say the second OTE share float may occur in two instalments, including a share capital increase in the second. The national econy ministry is looking into the option.
--The new economic crimes squad is to receive powers that will allow it access to banks and the Athens bourse.
--A new adviser is to be appointed to give evaluations on energy and transport projects, the national economy ministry announces.
--The electricity company DEH expects profits of 99 billion drachmas (19.3 percent) in 1997.
KERDOS

--Farmers and the government are on course for collision with the promise of a new period of trials for producers and the economy looming larger than ever, with the beginning today of the second round of farmers' protests.
--Salomon Brothers warned yesterday that a further fall in interest rates would mean exchange risks for the drachma.
--The national economy ministry expects a further drop in inlfation this month to 7.1-7.2 percent, according to figures available. The drop is due to stabilised prices for basic goods and services.
EXPRESS
--The distribution of natural gas has stalled at the squabble between DEPA and DEFA over the final settlement of DEFA's 18 billion drachma debt.

--New evaluation advisers for projects in the energy and transport sectors - tenders were announced yesterday - are expected to give a significant boost to the national economy ministry, Deputy Minister Christos Pachtas says.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Battle stations for government and farmers as the tractors roll out again.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
